name: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe 30B-A4B

lineage.how_derived: speech encoder (ASR + Sortformer-based speaker encoder) joined to the LLM and fine-tuned

purpose: Open-weight offline speech and audio model: audio plus a text instruction in, text out. NVIDIA's stated reasoning: the correct form of a transcript depends on audience and purpose, so one natural-language instruction per request selects the style instead of a convention fixed at training time. Tasks: transcription, translation, contextual and speaker-attributed transcription, language ID, word timestamps, audio QA.

license.name: OpenMDW-1.1
license.notes: licenses/ folder in the repo and LICENSE: OpenMDW-1.1 text read: "permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to deal in the Model Materials without restriction, including under all copyright, patent, database, and trade secret rights"; redistribution keeps the agreement and notices; outputs unrestricted. HF tag is "other". The repo also ships the Qwen3-ASR (Apache-2.0) and vLLM licenses for included parts.

architecture.kind: AUTOREGRESSIVE speech-augmented LLM: ~600M ASR encoder + ~99M Sortformer-based speaker encoder + hybrid Mamba-2/Transformer MoE decoder (decode is memory-bound like our LLMs)
architecture.drafter: MTP head (two trained depths, up to 8 speculative tokens) and separate DFlash2 draft model (word timestamps unavailable with DFlash2)
architecture.why_this_design: Promptable transcription: a speech-augmented LLM follows a per-request instruction (style, context, speaker attribution) instead of a fixed output convention (NVIDIA research page).

variants.format: GGUF, decoder 13.6 GB (Q2_0_M) to 19.7 GB (IQ4_NL), needs NeMo-Speech.cpp
variants.notes: sizes from research/52; engine claim from a secondary article

pc-16gb.notes: only the smallest GGUF, alone on the card

engine_support.notes: Upstream llama.cpp merged Nemotron 3.5 Lightning text support but has no audio path for this model (secondary source). Same decoder class as Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B, which research/49 lists as a coding candidate.

strengths: Best listed open-weight WER on English and multilingual Open ASR (vendor table, no independent evaluation at release)
German rated 'Leading' by the vendor, 2.81% mean
Speaker-attributed transcription and word timestamps in one model
Up to 1 hour per file, 65,536-token context
weaknesses: 30 GB class: no fit beside a coder on 16 GB
Rare generation loops, vendor recommends a post-processing guardrail
Word timestamps not available with DFlash2; first requests slow while kernels warm up
Open runtimes beyond vLLM/NeMo-Speech.cpp not confirmed
soft.behavior: Instruction-following speech LLM; reasoning toggle via chat template; audio understanding evaluated in English only.
best_for: Long German or multilingual meeting recordings with speaker labels on a 24-32 GB machine
avoid_for: 16 GB cards shared with a coding model
soft.maturity: NVIDIA, major vendor with regular releases; this checkpoint is about 6 weeks old (HF createdAt 2026-10-07).

user_reports.summary: The NVFP4 and FP8 repos linked from the card returned 404 at release; NVIDIA replied they would follow and they were live by 2026-11-01.
Community post: audio.cpp v0.9.4 runs it with about 7 GB VRAM using CPU offloading (not verified by us).

tona_fit.reason: Best independent German of any open model (2.79, all 8 sets, FP8 2.82; only commercial APIs are ahead), permissive OpenMDW license, built-in speaker attribution. Hardware: 14-20 GB at 4 bit, marginal on 16-24 GB classes, fine from 32 GB. Decoder is derived from Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B (Nemotron-H): a Tona Nemotron-H backend would serve it plus an audio encoder; until then NeMo-Speech.cpp / audio.cpp / vLLM.
blockers: no Nemotron-H backend and no audio encoder in Tona

sources.note: own research note, sizes of third-party GGUF
